office_does: The three Garfield County commissioners adopt the county budget, set county policy and ordinances, and oversee roads, property and services.
race_blurb: Commissioner Justin E. Dixon, on the board since 2015 and its 2026 chair, faces Gary W. Bowles, a Fire District 1 commissioner and volunteer EMT. Bowles led the district-only primary 171 to 165; every county voter votes in November.

candidates.summary: Second-term Garfield County Fire District 1 commissioner and volunteer EMT since 2010, running on transparency, open communication and collaboration.
highlights: Second term as a Fire District 1 commissioner; volunteer EMT since 2010 [S1]
Promises 'transparency, accountability, and open communication' and a government that 'keeps them informed' [S1]
Wants to 'move our county forward in a positive direction' [S1]

experience.basis: First-time county candidate challenging a commissioner of more than ten years, pitching honest leadership and moving the county 'forward'; has fire-district board experience, so not +2.

candidates.summary: Garfield County commissioner since 2015 and 2026 board chair, a farmer and rancher who sits on the state counties association's legislative steering committee and the Snake River Salmon Recovery Board.
highlights: Commissioner since 2015; won in 2018 and re-elected unopposed in 2022 [S1][S2][S3]
Chaired the board's March 2026 flood emergency proclamation [S5]
Washington State Association of Counties legislative steering committee; Snake River Salmon Recovery Board [S1]
Says 'fiscal responsibility, transparency, and accountability are essential' to maintaining services [S1]

experience.basis: More than ten years on the board, re-elected in 2018 and 2022, current chair, with state and regional board seats; runs on that record ('continue serving').

spending.basis: Single clear statement naming fiscal responsibility and accountability as essential to maintaining existing services; no expansion plank.
